analysis.title: Selective Memory: 2Q26 Semiconductor & Hardware Review
key_insights: JPM remains constructive on semiconductor fundamentals but more selective on credit. Strong operating performance has not produced consistent spread outperformance, and issuer-specific risks, financing technicals and relative valuations increasingly drive views.

Semiconductor spreads have diverged YTD. Larger AI infrastructure beneficiaries have widened the most, with Broadcom and NVIDIA widening particularly meaningfully amid scrutiny of AI financing structures and potential supplier obligations.
Per JPM's YTD spread table, AVGO '41 is +94bp wider and NVDA '40 is +71bp wider. The tightest names are DELL '38 at -32bp and AVT '28 at -31bp.

Outside AI, Intel and Marvell have tightened YTD and Dell has outperformed much of the AI-exposed universe. Qualcomm and NXP have widened modestly, and semiconductor equipment issuers have seen limited spread movement.

JPM is Overweight Intel, Marvell, Skyworks and Foundry JV Holdco. It is Underweight Broadcom, NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm, Texas Instruments, HP Inc, Arrow and Avnet. Analog Devices, Applied Materials, Dell, KLA, Lam, Microchip, Micron and NXP are Neutral.

JPM expects dispersion to persist, with incremental AI financing and greater scrutiny of capital commitments remaining important spread drivers despite healthy semiconductor demand and earnings growth.

AI financing structures are growing more complex. NVIDIA is partnering with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR on a $500bn financing platform. NVIDIA has agreed to residual value guarantees of up to 25% on certain transactions, implying maximum potential exposure of $125bn.

Broadcom supported a $35bn debt financing package for custom Google TPUs by guaranteeing customer payments. A follow-on is reportedly being marketed, with ~$42bn of senior secured debt backed by a Broadcom residual value guarantee and ~$18bn of junior debt led by Blackstone.

Oracle is reportedly in GPU financing talks with Apollo and Goldman Sachs. SpaceX is reportedly seeking ~$40bn ($30bn IG debt, $10bn bank loans). Broadcom is reportedly arranging more than $50bn of financing for custom accelerators developed with OpenAI. JPM views the Oracle arrangement as credit positive, though SpaceX's funding needs elsewhere could limit the benefit.

Last week's sharp selloff in CoreWeave debt and equity heightened scrutiny of debt-funded AI infrastructure. NVIDIA has the greatest direct exposure as CoreWeave's primary GPU supplier, equity investor and contracted capacity purchaser. Restructuring is not JPM's base case, but a severe liquidity event could disrupt capacity deployments and pressure chip orders.

JPM expects GPU-backed financing to accelerate in coming months, with NVIDIA, Broadcom and potentially AMD participating in additional transactions. Slower spending by major AI developers could pressure demand visibility across GPUs, networking silicon and memory, with continued hyperscaler investment as an offset.

Hyperscaler capex continues to accelerate. Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Microsoft are expanding multi-GW data center footprints and all four are developing custom ASICs, with Broadcom and Marvell as key partners. Amazon's chip business reached a $25bn run rate as of 2Q.

Inference is expected to become an increasingly important demand driver for GPUs, custom ASICs and networking silicon, though specialized architectures could intensify competition. HBM, server DRAM and advanced packaging demand extends capex benefits beyond accelerator suppliers.

Non-AI end markets are recovering unevenly. Automotive and Industrial are improving on inventory normalization and rising content per product. PC demand is mixed, and Mobile is weak because of higher memory costs and supply constraints expected to persist through 2027.
China is both a demand source and a risk. U.S. export controls, possible changes to export licensing and domestic Chinese competition matter most for advanced computing and equipment suppliers.

Intel's foundry progress on 18A and development of 14A are critical to securing external customers. Government incentives and supply chain diversification support U.S. semiconductor capacity investment.

market_movers.rationale: JPM prefers selective credits with sufficient spread compensation or improving fundamentals. Intel spreads have tightened YTD and Data Center revenue rose 59% y/y in 2Q.
Marvell spreads have tightened YTD. Data Center revenue grew 46% y/y to $2.17bn in 2Q with 3Q growth guided to about 75% y/y.
JPM keeps Skyworks Overweight as part of its preference for selective credits with adequate spread compensation.
Valuation concerns and an expectation of sustained AI financing pressure. Broadcom has widened meaningfully YTD amid scrutiny of its guarantee-backed financings.
Valuation concerns and sustained AI financing pressure. NVIDIA has the greatest direct exposure to CoreWeave and a $500bn financing platform with up to $125bn of potential guarantee exposure.
Valuation concerns and expected AI financing pressure. AMD may participate in additional GPU-backed financing transactions.
Qualcomm has widened modestly YTD. Handset revenue fell 20% y/y and the company guided F4Q handset revenue down 25% y/y.
JPM stays Underweight several mature semiconductor issuers with limited catalysts for meaningful tightening.

sector_views.rationale: Constructive on fundamentals but selective on credit. Spreads are driven by issuer-specific risk, AI financing technicals and relative valuations, favoring a selective rather than sector-wide approach.

earnings_insights: 2Q26 semis and hardware results (reported, vs StreetAccount consensus): NVDA revenue $96,221mn vs $92,280mn (+4.3%), EPS $2.22 vs $2.09, reported 8/26. Guidance: 3Q revenue above estimates, gross margins slightly below.
AVGO reported 9/2: revenue $29,591mn vs $29,240mn consensus (+1.2%), EPS $3.32 vs $3.22. F4Q revenue guidance slightly above expectations, operating margin slightly below.
MU reported 9/30: revenue $54,229mn vs $51,330mn consensus (+5.6%), EPS $33.42 vs $31.72. F1Q revenue and EPS guidance beat, gross margin guidance missed slightly.
INTC reported 7/23: revenue $16,128mn vs $14,430mn consensus (+11.8%), EPS $0.42 vs $0.22. 3Q revenue, gross margin and EPS guidance all above Street.
DELL reported 9/3: revenue $46,971mn vs $44,930mn consensus (+4.5%), EPS $7.04 vs $4.91 (+43.4%). 3Q revenue and EPS guidance ahead, prior FY27 guidance raised.
AMD reported 8/4: revenue $11,536mn vs $11,310mn consensus, EPS $1.66 vs $1.62. 3Q revenue and gross margin guidance both ahead of estimates.
MRVL reported 8/27: revenue $2,739mn vs $2,720mn consensus, EPS $0.80 vs $0.93 consensus (-14.0%). F2Q revenue, gross margin and EPS guidance all above consensus.
QCOM reported 7/29: revenue $9,947mn vs $9,690mn consensus, EPS $2.21 vs $2.24 (-1.3%). F4Q revenue guidance slightly above consensus, EPS guidance below.
TXN reported 7/22: revenue $5,463mn vs $5,250mn consensus (+4.1%), EPS $2.14 vs $1.94. 3Q revenue and EPS guidance both above estimates.
HPQ reported 8/26: revenue $15,677mn vs $14,390mn consensus (+8.9%), EPS $0.83 vs $0.66. Prior FY26 EPS and FCF guidance raised.
AVT reported 8/5: revenue $8,295mn vs $7,560mn consensus (+9.7%), EPS $2.28 vs $1.80. ARW reported 8/6: revenue $9,992mn vs $9,670mn, EPS $5.45 vs $4.59.

Other 2Q26 prints beat on revenue and EPS: KLAC EPS $1.05 vs $1.00, NXPI EPS $3.61 vs $3.52, SWKS EPS $1.08 vs $1.03, LRCX EPS $1.82 vs $1.69, MCHP EPS $0.76 vs $0.70, AMAT EPS $3.50 vs $3.40, ADI EPS $3.45 vs $3.34.

Broadcom Semiconductor Solutions revenue rose 127% y/y and 54% q/q to $20.1bn in F3Q. Management expects AI revenue to triple y/y to $21.7bn in F4Q, and AI semiconductor revenue to roughly double to $115bn in FY27 and reach $230bn in FY28.
NVIDIA Data Center revenue rose 117% y/y to $89bn in 2Q, with hyperscaler revenue doubling to $48.7bn. Vera CPU has about $20bn of demand and is in full production.
Micron Data Center revenue exceeded $34bn in F4Q. More than 75% of FY27 shipments are already committed, and FY27 capex is planned above $55bn.
Qualcomm Handset revenue fell 20% y/y to $5.1bn. It guided F4Q handset revenue to about $5.2bn, down 25% y/y, and expects Android revenue to decline about 20% this year, reducing EPS by $1.50.
Dell Client Solutions Group revenue rose 20% y/y to $15bn, driven mainly by pricing rather than units. Dell expects about 15% CSG growth in 3Q.
HP Personal Systems revenue rose 18% y/y to $11.8bn. Management expects a high-teens y/y PC market decline in 2H26 and below-seasonal F4Q Personal Systems revenue.

risk_factors: Contingent liabilities from GPU-backed financing, supplier guarantees and residual value guarantees, including NVIDIA's potential $125bn exposure.
A severe CoreWeave liquidity event could disrupt capacity deployments and pressure chip orders, with NVIDIA most directly exposed.
Slower spending by major AI developers could pressure demand visibility across GPUs, networking silicon and memory.
Tighter financing conditions among smaller, leveraged developers could constrain growth.
Memory supply constraints and higher component costs are weighing on Mobile and PC demand, expected to persist through 2027.
U.S. export controls, licensing changes and Chinese domestic competition for suppliers with China exposure.
Specialized inference architectures could intensify competition for GPUs.

geopolitical: U.S. export controls and broader trade restrictions pose risks for semiconductor suppliers with meaningful China exposure.
Potential changes to export licensing requirements and competition from domestic Chinese manufacturers are considerations for advanced computing and equipment suppliers.
Government incentives and supply chain diversification efforts support U.S. semiconductor manufacturing investment, including Intel's foundry strategy.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler capex is accelerating, AI demand is strong and well-capitalized hyperscalers should keep supporting underlying demand. NVIDIA cites redeployability, IG counterparties and substantial FCF as mitigants.
tension_points.bear_case: GPU-backed financing, supplier guarantees and residual value guarantees raise contingent liability questions. The CoreWeave selloff intensified scrutiny, and NVIDIA and Broadcom have widened the most YTD.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A severe CoreWeave liquidity event that disrupts capacity deployments and pressures chip orders, or slower spending by major AI developers.

theme_stances.key_argument: Financing risks are becoming increasingly important as GPU-backed financing and supplier guarantees raise questions on contingent liabilities.
